Backdrop

Backdrop draws the MixOS desktop background. It is its own program, not part of the compositor: it puts one surface on the compositor's background layer for each output, under every window and panel, and draws it with egui. A crash in it never takes the session down.

What it draws today:

  • a solid colour per output, or the session theme's colour when no document names one;
  • a PNG or JPEG image, with fill, fit, centre, tile or stretch sizing;
  • a slideshow, from a folder or an explicit image list, with a half-second crossfade. Each output may have its own wallpaper.

The live folder view remains planned. The probe (backdrop --probe) is the regression gate for the surfaces, scale and input, and draws its own labels.

The document

backdrop.mx (strict data, schema: 1), in the app's config directory (AppDirs, config/backdrop.mx) unless --config PATH names another.

schema: 1
default: { colour: "#1e1e2e" }
outputs: {
  "DP-1": { image: "/usr/share/wallpapers/hills.jpg", fallback: "#000000" },
}
  • schema is required and must be 1.
  • default is one wallpaper; without it the session theme's colour fills every output.
  • Each wallpaper names exactly one of colour (#RRGGBB, six hex digits), image (an absolute path) or slideshow (the source and timing below). fallback (#RRGGBB) goes with an image or slideshow: it shows behind transparent pixels and in letterbox bars. Without it the theme colour shows.
  • fit goes with an image or slideshow. It defaults to fill, which crops equally from opposite edges to cover the output. fit preserves the aspect ratio with letterbox bars; centre centres the image at its native pixel size; tile repeats at its native pixel size from the top left; stretch covers the output without preserving the aspect ratio. Native sizing honours the output scale even when the retained texture has been downscaled.
  • outputs maps an output's name (DP-1) to its own wallpaper; an output without one takes the default.
  • Unknown keys, wrong types, bad colours, relative paths and other shapes are refused, naming the field. A bad document at start stops the app.

Command line: --colour #RRGGBB or --image FILE replaces the document's default for this run (it is not stored). --service NAME registers the Bus name (default backdrop).

Slideshows

schema: 1
default: {
  slideshow: { folder: "/usr/share/wallpapers", interval_s: 600, shuffle: false },
  fallback: "#101820",
  fit: "fit",
}

Replace folder with images: ["/usr/share/wallpapers/a.png", "/usr/share/wallpapers/b.jpg"] for an explicit order. Exactly one source is required, all paths are absolute, and an explicit list must be non-empty. interval_s defaults to 600 and values below 5 are refused. shuffle defaults to false. Folder discovery is bounded and non-recursive; PNG and JPEG files are sorted before scheduling. Discovery and decoding run on the worker. The folder is discovered at startup or on a set; reapply the document to pick up folder changes. Repeated paths in a list share one schedule entry.

A slideshow retains its current image while the next decodes. A failed decode keeps that image and reports the error; the failed entry is skipped on the next attempt, which waits for the interval. Entries are tried again on later cycles. A successful advance crossfades for about 0.5 seconds, then releases the previous image and texture. The configured source is preserved when stored. A refused replacement also defers active slideshows for another interval, so their last good image stays visible after the refusal.

Images

  • PNG and JPEG only. The file is opened once, without blocking (a FIFO or device is refused), and read through a limit of 32 MiB; anything larger is refused. The format, the header's dimensions and the pixels all come from those same bytes. A header over 16384 pixels a side, or over 32 Mpx, is refused before any pixel buffer exists. The decoder's own allocation cap is 256 MiB.
  • Decoding runs on one worker thread, one image at a time. The kept image is downscaled so its longest side is at most 3840 pixels.
  • At most four resident image sources per document, counted after command-line overrides. A slideshow counts as one source regardless of its list length; only its selected images are decoded.
  • Every image a set names is decoded again, even one already on screen, so a file replaced at the same path is picked up by the next set.
  • A set applies only once all its images are decoded. A missing, corrupt, oversize or unsupported image refuses the whole change: the last applied backdrop stays on screen, and the reason is in backdrop.state. Images being kept for a refused or superseded set are dropped at once; in-flight results are discarded on completion.

Memory budgets

Two aggregate budgets, both enforced; the per-image limits above are not totals.

BudgetLimitWorst case
Decoded RGBA held by the controller (applied and candidate images together)512 MiB (RESIDENT_BUDGET)a decode that would take the total over it is refused (IMAGE); the last applied images stay until a whole candidate set applies
Accounted wallpaper texture bytes, across all outputs, overlap included (TEXTURE_BUDGET)512 MiBfour full-size outputs swapping (four old and four new textures)

Each output keeps its own texture at the decoded size, capped at 3840 pixels a side. The budget can leave additional outputs on fallback when there is no room for their textures. An image over the device's texture-size limit keeps the output's last good image on screen, or shows fallback when there is none, with the limit reported in that output's error.

A full-size image is 3840 × 3840 × 4 bytes = 56.25 MiB, the largest kept. Four applied plus four candidates is 450 MiB, which fits the 512 MiB resident budget. Textures are accounted as the bytes of the new size reserved while the old is still held, so a swap is counted in full. When bytes are released, live outputs are woken once so one that was starved draws again; nothing wakes when nothing is freed.

  • A context owns one image texture, or two during a slideshow crossfade. Replacing it reserves the new size while the old is still held, so the overlap is counted; a texture that does not fit leaves that output on its fallback colour, with the reason in its error. Removing an output, showing a solid colour, or a change of image releases its bytes.
  • A texture upload copies the decoded image once (a transient copy of at most one image, on the CPU).

These account for wallpaper data, rather than total process RSS or GPU-driver memory. Compressed input, decoder allocations, RGBA conversion and resizing have their own transient bounds; the renderer also owns resources beyond the wallpaper textures.

The Bus

Service backdrop (or --service). Commands (registered in docs/docs/spec/bus/commands.conf.mix):

CommandClassBodyReply
backdrop.pingquery{}{schema, service}
backdrop.statequery{}the state below
backdrop.setintenta complete document (above)the change, once applied
backdrop.nextintent{}full state, once the next images have decoded and applied

backdrop.set replaces the whole document; it does not patch it. A valid set waits for its images, is stored in the document's file (atomically, through config::atomic), and then applies. Its reply is rc 0 with {requested, active, config_file}. A refusal is rc 10 with {error_code, message}:

  • ARGUMENT: the body is not a valid document (nothing changed);
  • IMAGE: an image did not decode (nothing changed);
  • STORE: the document could not be stored (nothing changed), or it was stored but its durability is not confirmed (applied; the reply says so);
  • SUPERSEDED: a newer set replaced this one before it applied.
  • BUSY: a next arrived while a set or advance was decoding;
  • NON_SLIDESHOW: a next was requested with no applied slideshow;
  • UNKNOWN_COMMAND: the requested command is unknown; the reply includes its command name.

backdrop.next advances configured slideshows without changing or storing their sources. It refuses a configuration with no slideshow. An advance waiting for decode keeps the current pixels; a newer set can supersede it. Refused advances are not published as executed commands. Automatic advances run independently for each configured source and wait for the active crossfade to finish. A corrupt image on one output does not stop other outputs' schedules. A manual next advances all slideshows together and can interrupt their current fade.

backdrop.state answers with no output on screen: {schema, service, requested, active, pending, error, config, config_file, outputs, fit, slideshows}. fit is the default image's effective fit (or null for a solid fill); outputs also report their effective fit. Each slideshow reports its output (null for the default), current_path, index, count, interval_s, shuffle, pending and fading. requested and active are revisions: requested numbers every request, including startup and automatic slideshow advances, made, and active is the revision of the accepted configuration. pending is the revision still decoding, if any. error is the last refused change's reason until another change applies successfully, including an automatic advance. outputs lists each output drawn so far, with its size, scale, what it shows (theme, colour, image or fallback), its error, and presented_revision: the revision that output last drew. Use that field to see what is on screen; active alone does not mean every output has presented it yet.

Every applied Bus set or next is one run of its command and is published on backdrop.action.executed with origin bus. The command line's default is not a run: it is the start state.

Cost

It costs nothing while nothing changes. A static colour or image draws once per output and then sleeps; a set, a decode, a change of output or scale wakes it through egui's repaint request.

The slideshow controller waits on its inbox until the next schedule or fade deadline. It never polls. Repaints run only while a fade is active, and stop when the previous texture is released.

Start-up and failure

  • The Bus registration must succeed: if the broker refuses or is unreachable, backdrop exits with the reason rather than running a second, unregistered wallpaper.
  • An output that goes away is released (LayerProgram::removed): its context, its texture and its status.

Known gaps

  • The theme's colour is taken from the installed style's panel fill, not a named design token. Naming the desktop token is a follow-up.
  • Overlapping sets (one still decoding when the next arrives) are exercised by the controller's unit tests; the Mix gate sends its sets one after another.
  • Input limits bound allocations, not filesystem latency. A stalled mount can block the single decode lane until its I/O returns; state, ping, theme and solid-colour controls remain available. Superseded in-flight results are discarded on completion; already queued jobs are withdrawn immediately.

Running it

Run it inside a MixOS session: backdrop, or backdrop --colour #1e1e2e, or backdrop --image /abs/path.jpg --service backdrop-test.

Source layout

The source is apps/backdrop:

  • src/main.rs: command line, the start-up document, the layer loop;
  • src/control.rs: the Bus controller and its one command, backdrop.set;
  • src/program.rs: the layer program, which only draws a published view;
  • src/probe.rs: --probe, the regression probe (JSON lines on stdout);
  • crates/wallpaper: the engine: the document, colour, fit, decode limits and revisions. Pure data, no Bus and no window.

Tests

Building and the cargo tests are not in this tree's checks yet; the cargo gate runs on a build worker. cargo build -p backdrop enables toolkit's layer feature.

  • tests/desktop/wallpaper_gate.mix runs the wallpaper on a private broker and a private nested compd, takes screenshots of a solid colour and a PNG (share/brand's favicon), and checks backdrop.set and backdrop.state: a refused image keeps the last good pixels and revision, rapid sets apply in order, a non-document is refused, the accepted document is stored, and the process is idle. Run it from the checkout; --image-fixture PATH names a different PNG and --shot-out DIR keeps the PPMs.
  • tests/desktop/backdrop_gate.mix is the --probe regression gate: input, paint and occlusion. It runs the probe on a private nested compd and checks the band, the paint, the screen, click delivery and occlusion: mix tests/desktop/backdrop_gate.mix --bin <compd> --config-file tests/desktop/smoke-settings.json. On a build worker add --software --private-bus --noded <noded>.
  • Unit tests (cargo test -p wallpaper, cargo test -p backdrop) cover the document, colour, fit, decoder limits (including an oversized header and a FIFO), revisions, candidate and active images, the texture budget and the command registry.
